# Slider

A value picked by dragging along a track, when an exact number is not needed.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill odv-pill-out">Left out of Accessible first</span> The scheme avoids widgets that need drag or precise pointing. A person with a tremor completes a form here, and an exact answer is typed. <span class="odv-instead">Use instead: <a href="./input">Input</a>, <a href="./radio-group">Radio group</a></span></p>

## When to use it

- **Use it when:** Volume, brightness, a rough range; pair with a number field when precision matters.
- **Not when:** An exact answer people must type.

Instead:

- [Input](./input.md): An exact number.
- [Radio group](./radio-group.md): A few named choices.

## Words

- Use common words. Explain any term you must use.
- One idea per sentence. Put the action first.
- Never blame the person.
- Use: Continue, Change, Start, You. Avoid: Invalid, Utilise, Submit, Error code.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Continue
- `content.action.cancel`: Go back
- `content.action.destroy`: Delete
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Start a new application

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

| Keyboard | What happens | Not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| undefined | Arrow keys change the value; Home and End jump to the ends. | undefined |

Test before you ship:

- [ ] It has a name and announces its value. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add slider
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Tokens it reads

Slider reads 13 tokens of its own, each an alias of a semantic token. Each row is one part: its own token, the semantic it aliases, and the value it ends at. Change a semantic and every component that reads it follows; override one of Slider's tokens to change Slider alone.
